trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out right or down yet, so I'll make an educated guess: right.
I can't rule out left or down yet, so I'll make an educated guess: left.
Going left would wall in number 10, the last number. So the line goes down.
Going left would cut off the top-left corner (2 cells); going right, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes down.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going left would cut off the top-left corner (3 cells); going right leaves no safe move afterwards; going down, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So my guess (left from cell (2,3)) was wrong, so the line must go down.
Going left, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,2). So the line goes down.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going left, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves; going to number 2, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,5). So my guess (right from number 1) was wrong, so the line must go down.
Going left would wall in number 10, the last number; going right leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes down.
Going left would cut off the top-left corner (2 cells); going right, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes down.
Going left would cut off the top-left corner (3 cells); going right, the next 4 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,5). So the line goes down.
Going left would leave both cell (4,1) and cell (6,1) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes right.
Going down would force the line onto number 9 before its turn; going right, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at number 3. So the line goes up.
Number 3 is only reachable this way.
Going right leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes down.
Going down would cut off the left side (8 cells). So the line goes right.
Going down would leave both cell (6,4) and cell (6,6) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going right would cut off the bottom-left corner (11 cells). So the line goes up.
The line must go up: right is number 8, which comes later.
Going right would force the line onto number 8 before its turn. So the line goes up.
Going right would leave both cell (1,6) and cell (3,6) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going up would cut off the top edge (6 cells). So the line goes left.
Going left would leave both cell (1,3) and cell (3,3) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
